The early life stages of the Long whiskers catfish Mystus gulio are characterized by a remarkably low neonatal mass, with newly emerged yolk-sac larvae weighing approximately 0.0014 grams [Wwb = approximately 0.0014 grams]. This minute size, estimated from the oocyte diameter of a congeneric species, reflects an initial endowment of yolk that sustains the lecithotrophic larva through the period of chorionase secretion and eclosion. Following the rapid absorption of the yolk reserves and the onset of exogenous feeding, these prolarvae embark on a period of accelerated growth. Under captive rearing conditions maintained at a stable 25 °C [T = 25 °C], the maximum reproductive output recorded for this species has been estimated from a combination of spawning observations. Females deposit approximately 64 eggs per clutch [N_R_i = approximately 64 eggs per clutch] and, given the thermal regime, are capable of completing a spawning event roughly once per day [F_R_i = event roughly once per day], a remarkably high frequency that underscores the opportunistic reproductive strategy of this tropical bagrid catfish.

As individuals transition from the actively growing juvenile phase toward reproductive maturity, a key milestone is reached when the total length attains 20 centimeters [Lp = 20 centimeters]. This measurement, designated as the total length at puberty, represents the size threshold at which gametogenesis is initiated and the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis becomes fully activated. Correlated with this length is the wet weight at puberty, which has been estimated at 87 grams [Wwp = 87 grams], a body mass that reflects the accumulation of sufficient body reserves to support the energetic demands of vitellogenesis and spermiation onset. The relationship between length and mass in this species follows a typical power-law growth trajectory, and the attainment of this pubertal threshold generally occurs within the first year of life under productive conditions. Sexual maturation in Mystus gulio thus represents a size-dependent rather than strictly age-dependent process, consistent with patterns observed in many iteroparous tropical teleosts that face variable food availability and predation pressure within their estuarine and freshwater habitats.

The ultimate size that a Long whiskers catfish can achieve under favorable environmental conditions is defined by its asymptotic total length of 46 centimeters [Li = 46 centimeters]. Corresponding to this maximum recorded length is the ultimate wet weight, which reaches approximately 1100 grams [Wwi = approximately 1100 grams], a substantial body mass that places Mystus gulio among the larger members of its genus. Attaining such a size requires several years of sustained growth, and during this period the fish must balance the competing energetic demands of somatic expansion with the ongoing costs of basal maintenance, routine activity, and, once pubertal, periodic reproductive investment. Field surveys of older individuals indicate that growth rates decelerate markedly after the onset of maturity, with asymptotic size being approached gradually rather than abruptly. The capacity to reach this maximum length is contingent upon access to productive foraging grounds and the avoidance of size-selective mortality, factors that may vary considerably across the species' distribution in Southeast Asian river systems and brackish coastal zones.

Longevity in Mystus gulio has been documented from mark-recapture studies conducted in natural habitats. The oldest individuals recorded attained a lifespan of approximately 1460 days [am = approximately 1460 days] under ambient thermal conditions typical of their native range, which averaged 27.6 °C [T = 27.6 °C]. This maximum lifespan, equivalent to roughly four years, is consistent with the moderate longevity expected for a tropical bagrid catfish of its body size. The completion of the lifespan in such individuals is generally associated with the progressive deterioration of physiological function and the eventual failure of vital organ systems, rather than being triggered by a single catastrophic event. Comparative data from captive populations suggest that individuals held under protected conditions with ad libitum feeding and absence of predators can occasionally exceed this typical maximum, though the wild-recorded value of about four years likely represents the ecological norm for this species in Southeast Asian freshwater and estuarine environments.

Reproductive output in this species is strongly influenced by body size, such that larger females are capable of producing more clutches over the course of a single spawning season. The total length at puberty of 20 centimeters [Lp = 20 centimeters] serves as the lower bound for reproductive participation, while the asymptotic length of 46 centimeters [Li = 46 centimeters] defines the upper limit of reproductive potential. Between these two endpoints, fecundity scales positively with body mass, and a female that has attained the ultimate wet weight of 1100 grams [Wwi = 1100 grams] is capable of sustaining the high daily spawning frequency documented under optimal thermal conditions. Age-related mortality, with a maximum documented lifespan of 1460 days [am = 1460 days] at the prevailing temperature of 27.6 °C [T = 27.6 °C], imposes a temporal constraint on lifetime reproductive output, such that early maturation and rapid growth are strongly favored by natural selection in this short-lived, iteroparous species inhabiting variable tropical waters.
